name: Quantum volume certification
summary: Quantum volume per Cross et al. 2019: finite-shot heavy outputs, the 2-sigma pass rule, per-width intervals, achieved QV and a report.
description:
Runs the quantum volume protocol of Cross, Bishop, Sheldon, Nation and Gambetta (2019) on a simulated device over a list of widths. For every width it draws the square model circuits of Haar-random SU(4) layers (the open SDK's circuits and ideal distributions), mixes each ideal output distribution toward uniform with the depolarizing rate, samples a finite number of shots per circuit and counts heavy outcomes, those above the ideal median. The certification applies the protocol's rule exactly: the mean heavy-output probability over circuits must exceed 2/3 by two binomial standard deviations, h - 2 sqrt(h(1-h)/n_c) > 2/3. Beside that rule it reports a 95% interval from the empirical spread across circuits and a bootstrap interval, the mean ideal and exact noisy heavy-output probabilities for reference, the achieved quantum volume 2^(largest passing width) with a flag saying whether every smaller tested width also passes, whether the circuit count meets the protocol's minimum of 100, and a Markdown report.

For people who want the certification rule applied as published, with its statistics visible, as a reference for a device run or for teaching.

This is a KetQat Pro product: it runs locally like every catalog product, from a signed bundle installed with `ketqat pro install` under a time-limited entitlement. Its implementation is not part of the open SDK.
useCases: Apply the published quantum volume pass rule to simulated heavy-output counts at several widths and read off the achieved QV
See how shots, circuit count and depolarizing strength move a width from pass to fail
Check a hand-computed or device-side certification against a reference implementation of the rule

inputs.name: widths
inputs.description: Circuit widths m (and depths, since the model circuits are square), distinct.

inputs.name: circuits_per_width
inputs.description: Random model circuits per width; the protocol runs at least 100.

inputs.name: depolarizing_rate
inputs.description: Weight with which each circuit's ideal output distribution is mixed toward uniform (global depolarizing); 1 is a fully depolarized device.

outputs.name: achieved_quantum_volume
outputs.description: 2^(largest tested width that passes the rule); null when no tested width passes.

outputs.name: certification
outputs.description: passing_widths, failing_widths, max_passing_width, all_smaller_widths_pass, tested_widths and an interpretation sentence.

outputs.name: per_width
outputs.description: Per width: the rule's heavy_output_probability, binomial sigma, two_sigma_lower_bound and passed; empirical and bootstrap 95% intervals; mean ideal and exact noisy heavy-output probabilities; per-circuit heavy counts and seeds.

outputs.name: meets_protocol_minimum_circuits
outputs.description: true when circuits_per_width is at least 100.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Markdown report with the per-width table, the achieved quantum volume and caveats.

environment.resources: Defaults (widths 2, 3, 4; 100 circuits; 500 shots): well under a second on a 2024 Apple-silicon laptop (maintainer measurement); widths 2 to 8 at the defaults take about 0.5 s. Dense statevectors: circuits_per_width x sum(2^width) above 4000000 is refused before anything runs.

install: pip install "ketqat[pro,qinfo] @ git+https://github.com/ketqat/ketqat-sdk@<commit>#subdirectory=python" && ketqat pro login && ketqat pro install quantum-volume-certification@1.0.0

example.code:
import json
from ketqat_runner import catalog

record = catalog.run("quantum-volume-certification@1.0.0", seed=2026, widths=[2, 3], circuits_per_width=100, shots=500, depolarizing_rate=0.05)
result = record.result
print(json.dumps({
    "status": record.status,
    "achieved_quantum_volume": result["achieved_quantum_volume"],
    "all_smaller_widths_pass": result["certification"]["all_smaller_widths_pass"],
    "every_width_above_two_thirds": all(w["certification"]["heavy_output_probability"] > 2 / 3 for w in result["per_width"]),
}))

sampleResult.summary: Not generated in the open SDK: running this product needs a Pro entitlement and bundle, which this repository's CI does not have. Maintainer run of the private bundle with the defaults (widths 2, 3, 4; 100 circuits; 500 shots; depolarizing rate 0.05; seed 2026): heavy-output probabilities 0.7638, 0.8373 and 0.8254 with rule lower bounds 0.6789, 0.7635 and 0.7494, all passing; achieved quantum volume 16 with every smaller width passing; mean ideal heavy-output probabilities 0.7792, 0.8546 and 0.8408 (the asymptote (1 + ln 2)/2 = 0.8466 is not reached at width 2). At depolarizing rate 0.1 on the same seed width 2 fails marginally (bound 0.6641) while 3 and 4 pass, and the result says so.

assumptions: Model circuits as defined by Cross et al. (2019): width m, depth m, each layer a random permutation and Haar-random SU(4) on each pair; heavy outputs are those above the median of the ideal distribution.
Noise is a global depolarizing mix of each circuit's ideal distribution toward uniform, then finite-shot multinomial sampling; the heavy set is always defined by the ideal circuit.
The pass rule is the protocol's: mean heavy fraction over circuits minus two binomial standard deviations above 2/3.
scope: Widths 2 to 12, any number of circuits from 2 and shots from 1.
Per-width certification with binomial, empirical and bootstrap intervals; achieved quantum volume over the tested widths.
limitations: Global depolarizing is not a device noise model; the result is a check of the protocol and its statistics, not a hardware claim.
Quantum volume is claimed only for tested widths; untested widths are not inferred, and a non-monotone pass pattern is flagged rather than hidden.
The ideal heavy-output probability reaches (1 + ln 2)/2 only for large width; at width 2 it is about 0.78, so small widths pass with less margin.
Fewer than 100 circuits per width is below the protocol's minimum and is reported as such; the rule is still applied.
The implementation is delivered as a Pro bundle and is not open source; its validation tests live in the private repository, not here.
Tested on macOS and Linux only; Windows is untested.

origin.statement: Quantum volume, its model circuits and its pass rule are due to Cross, Bishop, Sheldon, Nation and Gambetta (2019); heavy-output generation follows Aaronson and Chen (2017); Haar-random unitaries are drawn by the QR method of Mezzadri (2007). The circuits and ideal distributions come from the open SDK's quantum_volume.py, and the sampling and statistics use NumPy. KetQat wrote the certification workflow: finite-shot heavy counts, the rule and intervals, the multi-width aggregation, the report and this catalog entry. KetQat did not invent the protocol or the rule.

pro.freeComparison: The open SDK already builds quantum volume model circuits with Haar-random SU(4), computes their exact ideal and depolarized heavy-output probabilities and, at one width, applies a 2-sigma bound from the empirical spread across circuits (quantum_volume.py). Nothing of that moves behind Pro, and this product calls those functions. Pro adds the certification as one catalog run: finite-shot sampling of heavy outcomes per circuit, the protocol's binomial 2-sigma rule as published, empirical and bootstrap intervals beside it, several widths with the achieved quantum volume and a monotonicity flag, the circuit-count minimum check, and a Markdown report.
